canonical_title: The Selected Letters of Philip K. Dick: 1972-1973
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: The Underwood-Miller volume for 1972-1973, covering PKD's move from Vancouver through the X-Kalay rehab community to a new life in Fullerton, the settling-in that immediately preceded the 2-3-74 events.
page_summary:
This volume of the Selected Letters covers 1972 and 1973, one of the sharpest hinges in Philip K. Dick's life. It opens in the aftermath of his troubled Vancouver trip and stay at the X-Kalay drug-rehabilitation community, follows his relocation to Southern California, and documents his settling into Fullerton, remarriage, and return to sustained work after the chaotic drug years of the late 1960s.

The letters show PKD rebuilding: corresponding with agents and editors, managing his precarious finances, keeping novels in print, and re-establishing a routine of writing. They record the relatively stable stretch that directly preceded the visionary rupture of February and March 1974.

As the Underwood-Miller edition for these years, the volume is the primary correspondence source for the transitional period between PKD's counterculture wreckage and the religious experiences that would dominate the rest of his life.
